clue.text: Protection against sun one put on head

indicators.note: one piece is placed on after the other, so it follows in an across answer

parts.note: the top is the head of something
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Advice to wear a hat in strong sunshine.
explanation.definitionFit: A topi is a lightweight pith helmet worn in hot countries to shield the wearer from sunshine.

clue.text: That is one way to move a barge

definitions.meaning: a formal phrase meaning namely or that is to say

definitions.text: one way to move a barge
definitions.meaning: a barge can be pulled along by a horse or tug, the boat being the 'it' hauled

explanation.surface: A remark on canal transport.
explanation.definitionFit: The first sense is the legal phrase meaning namely; split differently the letters describe hauling a barge with a rope.

clue.text: Sulkiness of girl, niece that is put out

parts.note: Petula is a girl's name, as in the singer Petula Clark

indicators.note: the letters are ejected from the word niece, leaving only what remains

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A moody young relative is in a huff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'girl, niece' suggests family members, but 'put out' is a deletion signal, not annoyance: the abbreviation for 'that is' is ejected from the niece, leaving NCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Petulance is childish sulky bad temper, the same peevish mood as sulkiness.

clue.text: It makes some people highly anxious

definitions.text: It makes some people highly anxious

parts.words: It makes some people highly anxious
parts.note: read literally, this is a condition making people anxious when they are high up, not merely very worried

explanation.surface: A vague description of something that causes great worry.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrophobia is the fear of heights, which makes sufferers anxious when they are high off the ground.

clue.text: Shackles donkey to pull on weed continuously

parts.note: chains are shackles for a prisoner
moke is British slang for a donkey

explanation.surface: A tethered donkey is made to tug at plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'weed' is slang for tobacco; MOKE is an old British word for a donkey.
explanation.definitionFit: To chain-smoke is to light one cigarette from another, puffing on tobacco without a break.

clue.text: State of surprise expressed, when one enters

indicators.note: the numeral goes into the exclamation, inside it

parts.note: oho is an exclamation of surprise
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone gasps as a visitor walks in.
explanation.definitionFit: Ohio is one of the states of the USA, in the Midwest.

clue.text: Emphasize two kinds of relief

parts.note: high relief is a style of sculpture where figures project boldly from the background
light relief is entertainment that eases tension

explanation.surface: A sculptor or comedian stresses different sorts of relief.
explanation.definitionFit: To highlight something is to draw attention to it, making it stand out.

clue.text: Brass is freely spent

definitions.meaning: brass instruments are played by breath, so a trumpet is a wind instrument sounded with the lips

explanation.surface: Money, called brass in slang, has been splashed out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brass' is also British slang for money, which tempts a single definition; here it is the family of instruments sounded by breath.
explanation.definitionFit: Brass instruments are sounded by breath, and money wasted on extravagance has been squandered in slang.

clue.text: Change covering degree duplicated in one's university

indicators.note: the change word wraps round the doubled degree, enclosing it

parts.note: to alter is to change

indicators.note: the degree is given twice in a row

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts degree

explanation.surface: A graduate amends a qualification listed twice at their college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' signals a container and 'duplicated' doubles the degree; an MA is the Master of Arts degree conferred by universities.
explanation.definitionFit: Alma mater, Latin for nourishing mother, is the usual term for the college or school someone attended.

clue.text: A block between banks in neoclassical style

parts.note: a dam blocks a river between its banks

explanation.surface: A building of graceful classical design stands by a river dam.
explanation.walkthrough: ADAM style is the elegant 18th-century neoclassical manner of the architect Robert Adam.
explanation.definitionFit: The Adam style is named after the Scottish architect brothers who designed in neoclassical taste.

clue.text: Having something attractive at home stableman found in old part of house

parts.note: with means having, as in a man with a hat
a draw is something that pulls in crowds
in means at home
a groom tends horses in a stable

explanation.surface: A stable hand is found at home with something alluring in an old house.
explanation.definitionFit: A withdrawing room, later shortened to drawing room, was the room in a grand old house where guests retired after dining.

clue.text: Composer's old sweetheart contributed to half of score

indicators.note: the sweetheart is added into the middle of the number, inside it

parts.note: a score is twenty, half of which is ten
leman is an archaic word for a lover

explanation.surface: A musician's former lover helped write half of a musical score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contributed to' puts LEMAN inside TEN; the 's of 'Composer's' stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Georg Philipp Telemann was a prolific German Baroque composer.

clue.text: Full house

parts.note: a gathering attended by every member of an assembly, rather than a winning poker hand

explanation.surface: A packed theatre or a poker hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A plenum is a meeting of an assembly with all its members present, a plenary session.

clue.text: Represent typical nag in theatrical performance

indicators.note: read as re-present, the letters are presented again in a new order

explanation.surface: An actor portrays a stereotypical scold on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Play-acting is performing in plays, and by extension pretending.

clue.text: Sidelined player's theatrical part

definitions.meaning: a footballer who plays out on the side is a wing, and 's turns this into the plural form
the areas at the sides of a stage, out of sight of the audience

explanation.surface: An injured footballer takes a small role in a play.
explanation.definitionFit: A wing is a winger in football, and the wings of a theatre are the offstage areas beside the stage.

clue.text: Tree making Hampshire naturalist smile

parts.note: Gilbert White wrote The Natural History of Selborne, a Hampshire village
to beam is to smile broadly

explanation.surface: A famous English nature writer grins at a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: Gilbert White was an 18th-century parson-naturalist of Selborne in Hampshire, an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: The whitebeam is a European tree with leaves white and downy underneath.

clue.text: Deficiency Alice certainly didn't experience

definitions.meaning: a deficiency is an amount by which something falls short
Alice in Wonderland tumbled a very long way down the rabbit hole

explanation.surface: Alice in Wonderland lacked something.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortfall is a deficit; read as two words it is a brief drop, unlike Alice's long fall.

clue.text: Bent on harming African country, fly over North

parts.note: Mali is a country in West Africa

indicators.note: the insect is placed over, covering, the compass point

parts.note: a gnat is a small fly

explanation.surface: A pilot flies over Africa intent on causing harm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' puts the insect around N, giving GNANT after MALI.
explanation.definitionFit: Malignant means wishing evil or intending to cause harm, malevolent.

clue.text: One absolutely controls it, as a rule

definitions.text: One absolutely controls it, as a rule

parts.words: One absolutely controls it, as a rule
parts.note: 'as a rule' seems to mean usually but describes a system of rule where one person holds absolute control

explanation.surface: A general observation about who is usually in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Autocracy is government by a single ruler with absolute power.

clue.text: Flexible choice essential in sport

indicators.note: something flexible bends into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: key means essential or crucial

explanation.surface: Being able to choose freely is vital in games.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flexible' rearranges CHOICE into ICEHOC, followed by KEY.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice hockey is a team game played on ice with sticks and a puck.

clue.text: King Edward, for example, seen in gallery with queen

parts.note: the Tate is a famous London art gallery
R stands for regina, queen

explanation.surface: A portrait of a king is displayed in an art gallery alongside a queen.
explanation.walkthrough: King Edward is a popular British potato variety, not a monarch here; TATER is slang for a potato.
explanation.definitionFit: Tater is informal for a potato, and King Edward is a well-known variety of potato.

clue.text: Union whose members are prepared to act

definitions.text: Union whose members are prepared to act

parts.words: Union whose members are prepared to act
parts.note: seems to describe militant workers ready for action but means performers who act for a living

explanation.surface: A trade union is ready to take industrial action.
explanation.definitionFit: Equity is the British trade union for actors and performers.

clue.text: Like diamonds, initially — or the whole pack

definitions.meaning: gems as first mined, before a jeweller shapes them
a deck of cards not yet divided by cutting

explanation.surface: A card player considers diamonds and the complete deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diamonds' and 'pack' suggest cards throughout, but the first sense is about gemstones.
explanation.definitionFit: Raw gemstones are uncut until shaped, and a card deck not yet split for dealing is also uncut.

clue.text: Namely haircloth carried by saint

indicators.note: the cloth is held within the abbreviation, inside it

parts.note: a cilice is a hair shirt or haircloth worn as penance

explanation.surface: A holy man wears a penitential hair shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carried by' signals the container; a cilice is the hair shirt worn by penitent saints, so the surface picture is apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Scilicet is a Latin adverb meaning that is to say, abbreviated sc.

clue.text: Gain ground

definitions.meaning: to secure or obtain, as in winning a contract
solid earth, as opposed to sea

explanation.definitionFit: To land a job is to gain it, and land is also terrain or the earth's surface.

clue.text: Out of steak, kitchen put back chicken dish

indicators.note: the extracted letters are put back to front
the letters are taken from inside the words steak and kitchen

explanation.surface: A cook throws out steak and serves chicken instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of' takes AKKIT from steAK KITchen; 'put back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicken tikka is a dish of marinated chicken pieces cooked in a tandoor.

clue.text: Oriental bowls like this, gaining top honours in sport

indicators.note: the sport takes in the cards, enclosing them

parts.note: RU stands for Rugby Union
the ace and king are the top honour cards in bridge

explanation.surface: Asian pottery wins prizes in competition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gaining' signals the container; 'bowls' suggests the lawn sport, and in bridge the ace and king are the top honours.
explanation.definitionFit: Raku is a Japanese lead-glazed earthenware, traditionally used for tea-ceremony bowls.

clue.text: This is it!

parts.note: the closing punctuation of the clue is itself what is being described

explanation.surface: A cry of excitement at a long-awaited moment.
explanation.definitionFit: The symbol at the end of the clue is the punctuation mark used after an exclamation.

clue.text: Study of some elements of mystery illness by Mark and others

parts.note: et al is Latin for and others
the lurgy is British slang for an unspecified illness

explanation.surface: A doctor called Mark and colleagues research an unexplained disease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The dreaded lurgy' is a British comic name for any vague infection.
explanation.definitionFit: Metallurgy is the science of metals, which are some of the chemical elements.

clue.text: Asian bird found in many parts

indicators.note: read as a verb, the word many is split apart and its letters reassembled

explanation.surface: A bird from Asia is common in many regions.
explanation.definitionFit: The myna is a starling-like bird of South and South-East Asia, noted for mimicry.
